subject: Formal Request for Copy of Personal Data (GDPR)
body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to formally request a copy of all personal data that your bank holds about me, in accordance with my rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). My customer reference number is C-1005.

In addition to a copy of my personal data, I would like to know how this information is used, including the purposes of processing, the categories of data concerned, and any third parties with whom it has been shared.

Please confirm receipt of this request and provide the requested information within the statutory timeframe of one month. Should you require any further verification of my identity, please let me know.

I look forward to your prompt response.

Yours faithfully,
Mark Ellison

draft.body:
Dear Mr. Ellison,

Thank you for your request for a copy of the personal data we hold about you, together with details of the purposes of processing and any third-party sharing. Your request has been forwarded to our Data Protection Officer, who will handle it and provide you with the final answer no later than 20 November 2026.

Requests to access, correct or erase personal data are not handled as ordinary complaints; they are forwarded to the Data Protection Officer the same day, and we will respond within one month [1].

If you are not satisfied with the outcome, you may turn to the Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület or the Magyar Nemzeti Bank (mnb.hu/fogyasztovedelem).

Yours sincerely,
Danubia Bank Complaints Team

retrieved.title: Danubia Bank – Card Disputes and Unauthorised Transactions Procedure
retrieved.content: Before the loss or theft of the card is reported, the customer may bear losses up to HUF 15,000, unless the transaction was made without strong customer authentication, in which case the customer bears no loss. Online transactions without strong customer authentication (SCA) are refunded in full.

retrieved.title: Danubia Bank – Complaint Handling Policy (internal), v4.2
retrieved.content: Customers flagged as vulnerable (for example elderly customers or customers in bereavement) receive plain-language answers without jargon, a direct phone contact, and priority handling. Their complaints are never closed without a human handler reading the full answer.

retrieved.title: Danubia Bank – Complaint Handling Policy (internal), v4.2
retrieved.content: When a complaint is rejected or partially rejected, the answer must inform the customer that they may turn to the Financial Arbitration Board (Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület) or to the Magyar Nemzeti Bank consumer protection service, and must include their contact details or links.

retrieved.title: Danubia Bank – Card Disputes and Unauthorised Transactions Procedure
retrieved.content: If goods or services paid by card were not delivered or were materially different from what was ordered, the customer should first contact the merchant. If the merchant does not resolve the issue, the bank initiates a chargeback through the card scheme. The chargeback is not a refund decision of the bank: the outcome depends on the merchant's response, typically within 45 days. The answer to the customer must explain that the chargeback was initiated, what documents are needed (order confirmation, correspondence with the merchant), and the expected timeline.

retrieved.title: Danubia Bank – Card Disputes and Unauthorised Transactions Procedure
retrieved.content: If a customer reports a card or account transaction they did not authorise, the bank refunds the amount immediately and at the latest by the end of the following business day after the report. The only exception is when the bank has reasonable grounds to suspect fraud by the customer and reports this in writing to the supervisory authority. The refund may not be delayed while the bank investigates the customer's possible negligence; liability is assessed afterwards.

assessment.rationale: This is a GDPR data-subject access request, not an ordinary complaint, and no transaction or fee is disputed, so no refund is due. Under complaint-handling-policy#6 such requests must be forwarded to the Data Protection Officer the same day, with the customer informed and a response within one month. This falls outside the standard complaint decision framework and requires specialist handling.

**Factual summary**

- **Customer:** C-1005, Mark Ellison (English-language), package PLUS, card ending 3310, account opened 2023-05-08, e-statements since 2023-05-08, no vulnerability flag.
- **Complaint type:** Data-protection request (GDPR access request), not a payment-service complaint. The customer asks for a copy of all personal data held, the purposes and categories of processing, and any third parties with whom data is shared, plus confirmation of receipt within one month.
- **Transactions/fees:** None referenced — the request cites no transaction IDs, amounts, dates or merchant, and no disputed fee code. No transaction or fee-rule lookups were therefore needed.

No further facts to collect; the request is a data-subject access request to be handled by the data-protection process.
